s: argon (a chemical element with an atomic number of 18).
trouble, an unpleasant or dangerous situation
The letter Ä in the German and Austrian spelling alphabets.
Die anderen Kinder ärgern ihn immer.
The other kids keep annoying him.
to be annoyed, to be angry, to get annoyed, to get angry
Ich ärgere mich über die hohen Preise.
I am angry over the high prices.

ärgern.et: Inherited from Middle High German argern (“worsen”), from Old High German argerōn, derived from arg (“bad”). Compare English eerie.

arg.et:
From Middle High German arc, from Old High German arg.
Compare Hunsrik aarich, Pennsylvania German arrig, Central Franconian ärch, and Dutch erg. Also etymologically linked is English eerie.

s: Der unerwartete Kurseinbruch war sehr ärgerlich für die Anleger.
The unexpected decline in share prices was very annoying for investors.
Der Verfall der Infrastruktur führt zu ärgerlichen Stromausfällen.
The degeneration of the infrastructure causes annoying outages.
Die Kundin wurde sehr ärgerlich, als sie den Betrugsversuch bemerkte.
The client became very annoyed when she detected the attempted deceit.
A female Argentinian, member of descendant of the people of Argentina
a wilful or intentional deceit or deception

Argwohn.et: From Middle High German arcwan, from Old High German argwan (“bad assumption, suspicion”); second element of compound is related to Wahn (“insanity”).

s: to argue (to bring forward an argument)

s: artlessness, innocence, simplicity of a person, simpleness, guilelessness
Sie stehen auf einem außerordentlich niedrigen Stande der Zivilisation, sind aber arglos und sehr friedsam.
They have an extraordinarily low status of civilization, but they are harmless and very peaceful.
Sie war vorsichtig im Detail, doch im Großen arglos.
She was careful in detail, yet unsuspecting overall.

Argusauge.et: Argus (“Argus”) + Auge (“eye”). A reference to the 100-eyed mythological Greek giant Argus.

Arglist.et: From Middle High German arclist, from Old High German arglist. By surface analysis, arg (“bad”) + List (“cunning, craft”).
